text: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai:
Speak now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people. Say to them:
Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how does it look to you now? Does it not seem like nothing in your eyes?

Yet be strong now, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD, and get to work, for I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts.
This is the covenant I made with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.

versions.text: For this is what the LORD of hosts says: In a little while, once more, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew order is 'once more (עוֹד אַחַת) — it is a little while.' Placing 'Once more' first preserves the emphasis of the Hebrew and reads with a stronger rhythm when spoken aloud.

text: I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come in, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.

versions.text: I will shake all the nations, and the treasure of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.
versions.explanation: The verb וּבָאוּ is plural, which supports a collective rendering ('treasures ... will come in'). A footnote could note the alternative reading 'the desire of all nations,' long understood messianically, since this is a well-known interpretive crux.

text: The silver is mine and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of hosts.
The glory of this latter house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts. And in this place I will grant peace, declares the LORD of hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Haggai:
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Ask the priests for a ruling on the law.
If someone carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and that fold touches bread or stew, wine or oil, or any other food, does it become holy? The priests answered, No.
Then Haggai said, If someone defiled by contact with a corpse touches any of these, does it become unclean? The priests answered, It becomes unclean.
Then Haggai replied, So it is with this people, so it is with this nation before me, declares the LORD, and so it is with everything they do; whatever they offer there is unclean.
Now think carefully about this, from this day backward: how things were before one stone was laid on another in the temple of the LORD,

versions.text: Now think carefully about this, from this day on: before one stone was laid on another in the temple of the LORD,
versions.explanation: Here the call to 'consider' looks back over the past (the following verses describe past crop failures), so 'from this day on' can mislead a listener into expecting a future reference. A backward-looking rendering, or a footnote on the Hebrew 'and upward,' clarifies the sense.

text: Ever since then, when someone came to a grain heap expecting twenty measures, there were only ten; when someone came to the wine vat to draw off fifty, there were only twenty.

versions.text: how did you fare? When someone came to a heap expecting twenty measures, there were only ten. When someone came to the wine vat to draw off fifty, there were only twenty.
versions.explanation: The phrase 'how did you fare?' is not in the Hebrew; it reflects an ancient version's reading of the difficult word מִהְיוֹתָם. If it is retained, a footnote should mark the Hebrew as uncertain; otherwise a rendering such as 'Ever since then' keeps closer to the received text and flows smoothly from verse 15.

text: I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight, mildew, and hail, yet you did not turn to me, declares the LORD.
Think carefully from this day on, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid. Think carefully:
Is there still seed left in the barn? The vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yielded. But from this day on I will bless you.
The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth.
I will overturn royal thrones and shatter the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother.

On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will take you, my servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, declares the LORD, and I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of hosts.
